summary: Google Flights HTTP 429 is an IP-level budget and must stay classified as a rate limit end-to-end: typed sentinel (no HTML in messages), slow bounded retry ladder, terminal rate-limited state (after a 429, a blocked envelope returns immediately without spending the blocked ladder, and later generic failures keep the rate-limit classification), no HTML fallback on 429, exit 7 with pacing + alternate-source hints on every Google-backed command including cheapest-longhaul's per-destination scan, and buffered partial output still delivered to --deliver sinks on failure.
reason: Bulk fare probes trip Google's per-IP rate limit; the generated error path embedded the raw HTML interstitial, bypassed rate-limit classification (generated classifyAPIError only serves AeroAPI commands), let a code-13 envelope after a 429 spend more budget on the HTML fallback, and left the dates fallback reading a rate-limited day range as clean success. The block frequently outlasts 15 minutes, so the fallback page is spent budget, not a fallback.
validated_outcome: unit tests cover the 429 ladder (2s/5s/12s), blocked-after-429 returning immediately as rate-limited, generic-after-429 keeping classification while context errors pass through, all-rate-limited dates fallback surfacing the sentinel, flushDeliver's three-way branching, and exit-7 classification; two independent multi-agent review passes (each with a cross-model adversarial reviewer) validated the contract; a live 429 during the 2026-07-24 dogfood session is the reproduction.
